title: Stationary Ground-Ball Fundamentals
primarySkill: Collecting a stationary football cleanly from ground level
objective: Introduce the fundamental body position, hand shape and movement sequence required to collect a stationary football cleanly and securely.
groundSize: Pairs operate within lanes approximately five metres long and three metres wide.
setup:
- Organise players into pairs.
- Place one football on the ground between each pair.
- Position the collecting player two metres from the football.
- The partner observes the technique and resets the football after each repetition.
- Mark a finishing cone one metre beyond the football.
- Players alternate after five repetitions.
- Begin at walking speed.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The collecting player begins in a balanced athletic stance.
2. The player walks towards the stationary football.
3. The final steps shorten as the player approaches.
4. The knees and hips bend to lower the body.
5. The head and chest remain over the football.
6. Both hands move towards the football.
7. The player collects it cleanly with two hands.
8. The football is brought securely towards the body.
9. The player continues through the finishing cone.
10. Partners reset and change roles.
coachingPoints: - Approach the football under control.
- Shorten the final steps.
- Lower through the knees and hips.
- Keep the head and chest over the football.
- Place the body behind its line.
- Present both hands early.
- Use the fingers rather than flat palms.
- Secure the football before rising.
- Continue moving after possession is established.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: - Whether the approach remains controlled.
- Whether the final steps shorten.
- Whether the player bends through the knees.
- Whether the body remains behind the football.
- Whether both hands collect simultaneously.
- Whether the football is secured before the player rises.
- Whether balance is maintained after possession.

commonErrors.error: The player bends only from the waist.| Lower through the knees and hips while keeping the chest strong.
commonErrors.correction: The head remains behind the football.| Move the chest and head over its line.

commonErrors.error: The player reaches with one hand.| Present two hands and collect through the centre of the football.
commonErrors.correction: The final approach is too fast.| Shorten the final steps and control momentum.

commonErrors.error: The football is lifted before it is secured.| Wrap both hands around it before rising.
commonErrors.correction: The player stops completely after collection.| Continue through the finishing cone under control.

progressions: - Move the starting cone further away.
- Place the football slightly left or right.
regressions: - Allow the player to start in a lowered stance.
- Use a larger or softer football.
- Practise the hand position without approaching.
successIndicators: - Lower through the knees and hips.
- Keep the body behind the football.
matchApplication: Clean ground-ball collection begins with correct body position. Players who lower effectively and place the body behind the football are more likely to maintain possession when the ball reaches ground level.
relatedDrills: - HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit
- MK-047 – Contested Mark and Ground-Ball Recovery

title: Body-Behind-the-Football Pickup
primarySkill: Positioning the body behind the football during collection
objective: Develop the habit of placing the body directly behind the football so a missed collection is stopped by the legs or torso rather than passing into dangerous space.
groundSize: Pairs operate in lanes approximately six metres long and four metres wide.
setup:
- Organise players into pairs.
- Place the football at the centre of each lane.
- Mark one central approach gate and two angled starting cones.
- The collecting player begins from the left, right or directly in front.
- The player must adjust the approach so the body finishes behind the football.
- The partner resets the football.
- Change roles after six repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The player begins from the nominated starting cone.
2. The collector approaches the football at controlled speed.
3. The running line is adjusted before the final two steps.
4. The player places both feet around or immediately behind the football’s line.
5. The knees and hips lower.
6. The head and chest move over the football.
7. Both hands collect and secure it.
8. The player continues through the central finishing gate.
9. The partner resets the football.
10. Repeat from all three starting angles.
coachingPoints: - Adjust the running line early.
- Avoid approaching from beside the football.
- Place the feet around its line where possible.
- Keep the chest behind and above the football.
- Use the body as a safety barrier.
- Present both hands.
- Secure possession before moving away.
- Continue through the central gate rather than drifting sideways.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: - Whether the approach angle is adjusted early.
- Whether the player arrives behind the football.
- Whether the feet support a balanced base.
- Whether the head remains over the football.
- Whether a fumble would be stopped by the body.
- Whether both hands secure possession.
- Whether the exit remains straight and balanced.

commonErrors.error: The player approaches from the side and reaches across.| Adjust the line earlier and move the body behind the football.
commonErrors.correction: The feet remain together.| Establish a balanced base around the ball line.

commonErrors.error: The player runs past the football.| Shorten the final steps and reduce speed.
commonErrors.correction: The chest remains upright.| Lower the hips and bring the head over the football.

commonErrors.error: The player collects outside the body line.| Reposition the feet so the hands collect centrally.
commonErrors.correction: The exit continues sideways.| Drive through the central finishing gate after possession.

progressions: - Add a passive opponent in front.
regressions: - Allow the player to stop before collecting.
successIndicators: - Position the body behind the football.
matchApplication: A player positioned behind the football remains competitive even when the first touch is imperfect. This is especially important in defence, wet conditions and contested situations.
relatedDrills: - HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit
- MK-047 – Contested Mark and Ground-Ball Recovery

title: Two-Hand Clean Ground-Ball Collection
primarySkill: Securing the football cleanly with two hands at ground level
objective: Develop strong and coordinated two-hand collection so the football is secured without bouncing between the hands or being knocked forward.
groundSize: Pairs operate four to six metres apart.
setup:
- Organise players into pairs.
- One player acts as the feeder.
- The feeder places or rolls the football slowly towards the collector.
- The collector begins two to three metres away.
- Score one point only when the football is secured with one clean two-hand action.
- Fumbles and body traps do not score.
- Change roles after ten feeds.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder places or rolls the football into the collection zone.
2. The collector approaches under control.
3. The player lowers through the knees and hips.
4. Both hands move towards the football together.
5. The fingers spread around its sides.
6. The hands close firmly at the same time.
7. The football is lifted slightly and secured against the body.
8. The player holds possession for two seconds.
9. The football is returned to the feeder.
10. Complete ten repetitions before changing roles.
coachingPoints: - Keep the hands relaxed before contact.
- Present both hands at the same height.
- Spread the fingers around the football.
- Collect through the centre rather than from one side.
- Close both hands simultaneously.
- Avoid slapping downward at the football.
- Secure it before rising.
- Hold the football firmly after collection.
- Judge success by first-contact control.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: - Whether both hands arrive together.
- Whether fingers wrap around the football.
- Whether one hand dominates.
- Whether the player pushes the football forward.
- Whether possession is secured before rising.
- Whether the football is trapped against the legs.
- Whether first-contact control improves.

commonErrors.error: One hand reaches before the other.| Present both hands together and close simultaneously.
commonErrors.correction: The player slaps the football forward.| Scoop around its sides rather than striking downwards.

commonErrors.error: The hands remain flat.| Spread and curve the fingers around the football.
commonErrors.correction: The player traps the football against the legs.| Collect cleanly in front and secure with the hands.

commonErrors.error: The football spills as the player rises.| Complete control before changing body height.
commonErrors.correction: The collector looks away after first contact.| Track the football until it is fully secured.

progressions: - Vary the football slightly left and right.
regressions: - Allow the player to pause before lifting.
successIndicators: - Wrap the fingers around the football.
- Secure it with one clean action.
matchApplication: Two-hand ground-ball collection provides the strongest first touch and prepares the football for the next disposal. Clean control becomes increasingly important under pressure and poor conditions.
relatedDrills: - HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit

title: Low-Body Pickup and Exit
primarySkill: Collecting the football from a low body position and exiting efficiently
objective: Develop the ability to remain low through the collection and accelerate away without standing upright too early or losing control.
groundSize: Lanes approximately eight metres long and four metres wide.
setup:
- Organise players into groups of three to five.
- Place the football at the centre of the lane.
- Mark a starting cone three metres behind it.
- Mark two exit gates, one left and one right, three metres beyond.
- The coach or feeder nominates the exit side as the player approaches.
- The collecting player remains low through the pickup.
- Rotate after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The player begins at the starting cone.
2. The collector approaches the football.
3. The coach calls the left or right exit.
4. The player shortens the final steps.
5. The knees and hips lower.
6. Both hands secure the football.
7. The player remains low for the first step after collection.
8. The outside foot plants towards the nominated gate.
9. The player accelerates through the exit with the football protected.
10. The next player begins when the lane is clear.
coachingPoints: - Lower before reaching the football.
- Keep the head over the collection.
- Secure the football with two hands.
- Avoid rising vertically after possession.
- Remain low through the first exit step.
- Plant with balance.
- Carry the football on the protected side.
- Accelerate only after control is established.
- Use both exit directions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: - Whether the player lowers early enough.
- Whether the football is collected cleanly.
- Whether the player rises too quickly.
- Whether the exit step remains balanced.
- Whether the correct gate is identified.
- Whether the football is protected.
- Whether acceleration follows control.

commonErrors.error: The player arrives upright and reaches down.| Lower the hips during the final approach steps.
commonErrors.correction: The collector stands straight up after possession.| Stay low through the first exit step.

commonErrors.error: The football is moved to one hand too early.| Maintain two-hand security until the direction change is complete.
commonErrors.correction: The exit plant is too long and unstable.| Use a shorter, stronger plant step.

commonErrors.error: The player exits towards the wrong gate.| Listen for the cue while maintaining football focus.
commonErrors.correction: The player accelerates before securing possession.| Complete control before driving away.

progressions: - Roll the football into the collection zone.
regressions: - Allow the player to pause after collection.
successIndicators: - Remain low through the first exit step.
matchApplication: Players must often collect the football and leave congestion immediately. Staying low allows quicker balance, direction change and protection from nearby opponents.
relatedDrills: - HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit

title: Moving Ground-Ball Pickup
primarySkill: Collecting a moving football while maintaining forward momentum
objective: Develop the ability to judge a rolling football, adjust the running line and collect cleanly without stopping before possession.
groundSize: Lanes approximately twelve metres long and five metres wide.
setup:
- Organise players into groups of three to five.
- Position the feeder at one end of the lane.
- The collector begins eight metres away.
- The feeder rolls the football into the lane at controlled speed.
- Mark a finishing gate beyond the collection area.
- The player must collect while moving through the lane.
- Rotate feeder and collector roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder rolls the football towards the collector.
2. The player tracks its speed and line.
3. The collector approaches at controlled pace.
4. The final steps shorten as the football nears.
5. The running line adjusts behind the football.
6. The player lowers through the knees and hips.
7. Both hands collect the football cleanly.
8. The player remains moving through possession.
9. The football is carried through the finishing gate.
10. Players rotate roles.
coachingPoints: - Track the football from the feeder’s release.
- Judge both speed and direction.
- Avoid sprinting beyond the collection point.
- Adjust the running line early.
- Shorten the final steps.
- Lower without stopping.
- Collect with two hands.
- Continue moving through the pickup.
- Secure possession before increasing speed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: - Whether the player judges the roll.
- Whether the approach speed is appropriate.
- Whether the running line finishes behind the football.
- Whether the body lowers while moving.
- Whether both hands collect cleanly.
- Whether the player stops before possession.
- Whether balance is maintained through the gate.

commonErrors.error: The player sprints past the football.| Reduce speed earlier and shorten the final steps.
commonErrors.correction: The collector approaches from beside the line.| Adjust early and place the body behind the roll.

commonErrors.error: The player stops before collecting.| Lower while continuing forward through the ball.
commonErrors.correction: The hands reach before the body is positioned.| Move the feet first, then collect centrally.

commonErrors.error: The football rebounds from rigid hands.| Relax before contact and wrap the fingers around it.
commonErrors.correction: The player increases speed before possession is secure.| Confirm control before accelerating.

progressions: - Vary the roll left and right.
regressions: - Allow the collector to begin closer.
matchApplication: Most ground balls continue moving after a spoil, poor kick or deflection. Players must adjust their feet and speed rather than treating every pickup as stationary.
relatedDrills: - HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit
- MK-047 – Contested Mark and Ground-Ball Recovery

title: Half-Volley Gather Fundamentals
primarySkill: Gathering a football immediately after it contacts the ground
objective: Teach players to gather a football cleanly on the first rise after the bounce by matching the hands to the football’s movement and maintaining the body behind the collection.
groundSize: Lanes approximately eight metres long and four metres wide.
equipment: Flat markers indicating the bounce zone
Optional junior-sized footballs for younger players
setup:
Organise players into pairs or groups of three.
Position the feeder at one end of an eight-metre lane.
Mark a bounce zone approximately one to two metres in front of the collector.
The collector begins three to four metres from the bounce zone.
Place a finishing gate two metres behind the collection point.
The feeder delivers a controlled downward bounce that reaches the collector on its first rise.
Begin with slow, consistent feeds before introducing variation.
Rotate the feeder after five repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The collector begins in an athletic stance and watches the feeder’s release.
The feeder bounces the football into the marked zone.
The collector moves forward and adjusts the feet to remain behind the football.
The player lowers through the knees and hips before the football reaches the ground.
As the football rises, the hands move forward and down to meet it early.
The fingers remain open, relaxed and directed around the football.
The player cushions the football into two-hand control rather than striking at it.
Possession is brought securely towards the body.
The collector rises in balance and moves through the finishing gate.
Players reset and repeat before rotating roles.
coachingPoints: Read the feeder’s release and identify the likely bounce point.
Reach the bounce line with the body, not only the hands.
Lower before the football rises.
Keep the head steady and the eyes focused on the lower half of the football.
Meet the football early on its first rise.
Place the hands behind and slightly around the football’s movement.
Cushion the football rather than attempting to trap it rigidly.
Secure possession before standing or preparing the next disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player identifies the bounce point early.
Whether the body arrives behind the football.
Whether the player lowers before the football rises.
Whether the hands meet the football rather than waiting at the body.
Whether the fingers remain relaxed and open.
Whether the football is cushioned into possession.
Whether the player maintains balance while rising.
Whether the collector remains confident after an unsuccessful attempt.

commonErrors.error: The player waits upright for the football to rise.
commonErrors.correction: Lower before the bounce and take the football closer to ground level.

commonErrors.error: The collector reaches with straight, rigid arms.
commonErrors.correction: Soften the elbows and allow the hands to travel with the football.

commonErrors.error: The player places the hands above the football.
commonErrors.correction: Position the hands behind and around its rising line.

commonErrors.error: The body remains beside the bounce line.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the feet so the chest finishes behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The player attempts to pin the football against the ground.
commonErrors.correction: Meet it on the rise and cushion it into the hands.

commonErrors.error: The player looks away before possession is complete.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain vision on the football until it is secured.

progressions: Vary the height and speed of the bounce.
Bounce the football slightly left or right.
Require the collector to continue running through the gather.
Add an immediate handball to the feeder.
Reduce the size of the bounce zone.
regressions: Use a larger and slower bounce.
Allow the player to begin closer to the bounce point.
Permit the player to start in a lowered stance.
Use a stationary football to rehearse hand shape.
Allow the football to bounce twice before collection.
Use a softer junior football for introductory groups.
successIndicators: Position the body behind the football.
Meet the football early with both hands.
Move smoothly into the next action.
matchApplication: A low kick, deflection or awkward handball may reach a player immediately after bouncing. Gathering the football on the half-volley prevents it rising into the body, passing underneath the hands or creating an opportunity for an opponent to contest possession.

title: Wide Ground-Ball Win to Corridor Switch
Ground-Ball Carry, Bounce and Deliver
primarySkill: Transitioning from a ground-ball collection into a controlled running bounce and disposal
objective: Develop the ability to collect a ground ball, accelerate into open space, complete a controlled running bounce and deliver accurately without losing running rhythm.
groundSize: Lanes approximately forty metres long and eight metres wide.
setup:
Mark a ground-ball collection zone eight metres from the starting cone.
Place a running-bounce gate twelve to fifteen metres beyond the collection point.
Position a disposal gate a further ten metres ahead.
Place a leading target fifteen to twenty-five metres beyond the disposal gate.
The feeder stands beside the collection zone.
The collector starts at the beginning of the lane.
The feeder rolls the football into the running path.
Rotate collector, feeder and target roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The collector accelerates towards the ground-ball zone.
The feeder rolls the football into the player’s path.
The collector gathers cleanly and secures possession.
The player accelerates into open space with the football carried in two hands.
Before reaching the running-bounce gate, the player transfers the football into a controlled bounce position.
The football is bounced and regained without breaking running rhythm.
The player scans the leading target.
The collector controls the final steps and prepares the kick.
The kick is delivered into the target’s path.
The player follows the disposal before roles rotate.
coachingPoints: Complete the collection before planning the running bounce.
Carry the football securely during the initial acceleration.
Choose a clear and balanced moment to bounce.
Push the football firmly towards the ground rather than dropping it.
Keep the bounce within the running path.
Regain two-hand control immediately.
Scan after securing the bounced football.
Control the final steps before kicking.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the initial ground-ball collection is clean.
Whether the player accelerates with secure possession.
Whether the bounce is completed at a suitable point.
Whether the football remains within the running path.
Whether the player regains two-hand control.
Whether vision lifts after the bounce.
Whether disposal preparation begins early.
Whether the final kick remains accurate.

commonErrors.error: The player prepares to bounce before securing the ground ball.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the collection and initial acceleration first.

commonErrors.error: The football is dropped rather than pushed towards the ground.
commonErrors.correction: Use a firm downward action in front of the running body.

commonErrors.error: The bounce moves outside the player’s path.
commonErrors.correction: Release it closer to the centre of the running line.

commonErrors.error: The player attempts to bounce at maximum uncontrolled speed.
commonErrors.correction: Select a balanced moment and control the stride.

commonErrors.error: Vision remains down after regaining the football.
commonErrors.correction: Lift the eyes and locate the target immediately.

commonErrors.error: The kick is rushed after the bounce.
commonErrors.correction: Use balancing steps before the ball drop.

progressions: Add a passive defender chasing from behind.
Vary the point at which the target begins the lead.
Introduce a decision between handball and kick.
regressions: Begin with the football in the player’s hands.
Rehearse the bounce separately before adding the ground-ball collection.
successIndicators: Complete a legal and controlled running bounce.
matchApplication: A player who wins a loose football in open space may need to carry beyond fifteen metres before disposing. Connecting the pickup, running bounce and kick allows territory to be gained without sacrificing control.
relatedDrills: GB-027 – Ground-Ball Win to Moving Lead

title: Scissor Support Ground-Ball Exit
primarySkill: Selecting between crossing support runners after a ground-ball collection
objective: Develop the ability to secure a ground ball, read two crossing support movements and release accurately to the runner who creates the clearest forward exit.
groundSize: Rectangles approximately twenty-five metres long and eighteen metres wide.
setup:
Mark a central ground-ball collection zone.
Position one support runner behind and left of the collector.
Position a second support runner behind and right.
Mark crossing lanes that pass behind or outside the collector before entering opposite exit gates.
Position the feeder behind the collection zone.
A coach displays a coloured marker that identifies which exit is restricted.
The collector must read the crossing runners and restricted gate.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls the football towards the central collection zone.
The collector approaches and scans both support runners.
Both runners accelerate on crossing lines.
The coach identifies one restricted exit gate.
The collector returns vision to the football and gathers cleanly.
The player protects possession while recognising which runner is moving towards the available gate.
The collector handballs into that runner’s path.
The receiver continues through the open exit.
The non-receiving runner becomes secondary support.
The original collector follows the possession through the middle.
coachingPoints: Scan the runner positions before lowering fully.
Support runners must cross with safe separation.
Return the eyes to the football before collection.
Secure possession before responding to the gate restriction.
Avoid predetermining the receiver.
Handball ahead of the runner rather than towards the crossing point.
The non-receiving runner must remain involved.
The collector should continue through the middle after disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the collector scans both runners.
Whether the crossing movements are safely timed.
Whether the restricted gate is recognised.
Whether vision returns to the football.
Whether collection remains clean.
Whether the correct runner is selected.
Whether the handball leads the receiver.
Whether all players continue supporting.

commonErrors.error: The collector chooses a runner before reading the gate.
commonErrors.correction: Wait for the full information before releasing possession.

commonErrors.error: Support runners cross too closely.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger the crossing times and maintain safe separation.

commonErrors.error: The player watches the runners and fumbles the football.
commonErrors.correction: Scan briefly, then return the eyes to the collection.

commonErrors.error: The handball is directed at the crossing point.
commonErrors.correction: Target the receiver’s movement beyond the crossing line.

commonErrors.error: The non-receiving runner stops.
commonErrors.correction: Continue as a secondary option.

commonErrors.error: The collector remains behind the play.
commonErrors.correction: Follow through the middle after disposal.

progressions: Add a passive defender closing the collector.
Allow the collector to carry through the middle if both runners are covered.
Introduce turnover transition after an inaccurate handball.
regressions: Operate with one support runner before adding the second.
matchApplication: Crossing support runs can confuse defenders and create an exit from congestion. The ball winner must process several moving options while still prioritising a clean ground-ball collection.

title: Spilled-Mark Ground-Ball Contest
primarySkill: Winning the football after it spills from a marking contest
objective: Develop the ability to anticipate a spilled mark, establish an effective crumbing position and compete for the ground ball against an opponent.
groundSize: Contest area approximately fifteen metres × twelve metres.
setup:
Position two players in a controlled marking contest.
Place one crumber from each team outside the immediate drop zone.
Mark a front-and-centre crumbing area.
The feeder kicks or throws the football to the marking contest.
The contest players deliberately spoil or bring the football to ground.
Crumbers compete for the spill using controlled body contact.
Mark two exit gates beyond the crumbing area.
Rotate marking and crumbing roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder delivers the football to the marking contest.
Contest players compete in the air under controlled conditions.
The football is spoiled or spilled to ground.
Both crumbers move from their starting positions towards the anticipated drop zone.
Players compete for body position and access.
The ball winner gathers with two hands where possible.
The player protects possession and exits through a gate.
The opposing crumber applies controlled chase pressure.
Marking players recover and become support options.
The group resets and rotates positions.
coachingPoints: Crumbers should begin outside the feet of the aerial contest.
Arrive as the football spills rather than standing beneath the contest.
Track the football through the marking players’ hands.
Establish body position before lowering.
Keep the head protected and eyes up.
Secure the football when available.
Exit away from the aerial contest.
Marking players must recover quickly after landing.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether crumbers begin in effective positions.
Whether arrival timing matches the spill.
Whether players watch the football through the contest.
Whether body contact is safe and legal.
Whether the ball winner collects cleanly.
Whether possession is protected.
Whether the exit moves away from congestion.
Whether marking players recover into support.

commonErrors.error: Crumbers stand directly beneath the marking contest.
commonErrors.correction: Begin outside the feet and arrive front-and-centre.

commonErrors.error: Players move only after the football hits the ground.
commonErrors.correction: Anticipate the spill and move as the aerial contest develops.

commonErrors.error: Crumbers watch the opponents rather than the football.
commonErrors.correction: Track the football through the hands and spoil.

commonErrors.error: Players dive into the feet of landing players.
commonErrors.correction: Remain balanced and enter the ground contest safely.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner turns back into the marking contest.
commonErrors.correction: Exit laterally or forward into space.

commonErrors.error: Aerial players remain out of the next phase.
commonErrors.correction: Recover immediately and become support or pressure.

progressions: Allow the aerial contest to determine the spill naturally.
Add a second crumber per team.
Add a scoring target after the exit.
Continue into a small-sided possession game.
regressions: Use a marking bag instead of live aerial contestants.
Use one active crumber and one shadow opponent.
Drop the football manually from shoulder height.
successIndicators: Time movement with the aerial contest.
matchApplication: Many marking contests do not result in a completed mark. Players positioned at ground level must anticipate the spill, compete strongly and either secure possession or prevent the opposition from exiting.

title: Wet-Football Pressure Collection
primarySkill: Securing a slippery football under controlled opponent pressure
objective: Develop the ability to adjust collection, protection and disposal technique when the football is wet or slippery and pressure reduces the available time.
groundSize: Lanes approximately twelve metres long and seven metres wide.
setup:
Lightly wet the footballs without making the playing surface unsafe.
Position the collector and defender five metres from the collection zone.
The defender begins one metre behind or beside the collector.
Mark two exit gates.
The feeder rolls or lightly bounces the wet football into the contest area.
Contact is limited to legal shoulder and hip pressure.
Inspect the surface throughout the activity.
Dry or replace footballs if they become excessively difficult to handle.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder introduces the wet football into the collection zone.
The collector and defender approach under control.
The collector positions the body between opponent and football.
The player gathers with two hands and absorbs the slippery football towards the body.
If the football spills, both players complete an immediate second effort.
The ball winner secures possession against the chest or protected hip.
The player exits through an available gate.
Where nominated, the player completes a short handball to a receiver.
The defender applies controlled pressure without taking the player to ground.
Players rotate roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Reduce approach speed slightly to improve control.
Lower early and present broad, relaxed hands.
Absorb the football into the body.
Expect the football to skid or slide.
Maintain two-hand contact longer than in dry conditions.
Do not attempt ambitious disposal before possession is secure.
React immediately to spills.
Keep the feet underneath the body on a wet surface.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether approach speed is adjusted.
Whether players maintain safe footing.
Whether hands remain relaxed.
Whether the football is absorbed towards the body.
Whether players react immediately to spills.
Whether possession is protected.
Whether disposal choices are realistic for wet conditions.
Whether surface safety remains acceptable.

commonErrors.error: The player attacks the wet football at excessive speed.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed earlier and control the final steps.

commonErrors.error: Hands are rigid and the football rebounds away.
commonErrors.correction: Relax the fingers and absorb the football into the body.

commonErrors.error: The collector tries to pick up with one hand unnecessarily.
commonErrors.correction: Use two hands and maintain contact longer.

commonErrors.error: The player stops after the first fumble.
commonErrors.correction: Continue immediately with a second effort.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner attempts an ambitious kick from poor balance.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and use the simplest effective disposal.

commonErrors.error: Players lose footing due to excessive drill speed.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce pace or stop the activity if the surface is unsafe.

progressions: Require a short wet-weather kick after collection.
Add a team score for consecutive retained possessions.
regressions: Use a lightly damp rather than fully wet football.
Allow the player to collect from a stationary start.
successIndicators: Absorb the football into the body.
matchApplication: Wet football reduces grip and changes bounce behaviour. Players must simplify their technique, remain balanced and expect second efforts rather than assuming the first collection will be clean.

title: Ground-Ball Pressure and Contest Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing ground-ball performance under controlled pressure, contact and congestion
objective: Assess each player’s ability to win, protect and release ground-ball possession across trailing pressure, body contact, congestion, numerical situations and fatigue.
groundSize: Six assessment stations arranged within an area approximately sixty metres × forty metres.
setup:
Establish six assessment stations:
Station 1: Trailing-pressure pickup and exit.
Station 2: Shoulder-to-shoulder contest.
Station 3: Boundary-pressure recovery.
Station 4: Congested extraction.
Station 5: Two-versus-one decision.
Station 6: Repeat-effort or fatigue extraction.
Assign a coach or trained observer to each station.
Pair players by size, skill and contact readiness.
Provide one familiarisation repetition at each station.
Use consistent feeds, starting distances and contact restrictions.
Record technical, tactical and safety outcomes separately.
Allow sufficient recovery between high-intensity stations.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players rotate through each assessment station.
Each player completes three scored repetitions per station.
Coaches assess movement before possession, contest technique, collection, protection and post-possession action.
Players receive no technical coaching during scored repetitions.
A repetition ends when possession exits the station, a turnover is completed or the coach stops the contest.
Unsafe contact or a feeder error invalidates the repetition.
Scores are recorded immediately.
Players rotate after every group member completes the station.
Coaches provide feedback only after the station or full circuit.
Results are used to identify individual and team development priorities.
coachingPoints: Apply the same contact restrictions to every player.
Assess safe body position before judging contest outcome.
Record whether the player seeks clean possession.
Evaluate ball protection and balance after collection.
Assess the quality and legality of disposal.
Record second effort after spills or lost contests.
Evaluate the use of support and numerical advantage.
Stop any repetition where fatigue compromises safety.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Approach speed and line.
Head and body position entering contact.
Legal use of shoulder and hip.
Clean collection where available.
Ball protection after possession.
Balance under pressure.
Second effort after a spill.
Recognition of support.
Disposal legality and effectiveness.
Transition after possession changes.

commonErrors.error: Contact intensity differs between stations or players.
commonErrors.correction: Standardise the permitted pressure before assessment begins.

commonErrors.error: Coaches score only the final possession result.
commonErrors.correction: Assess the complete process before, during and after the contest.

commonErrors.error: Players receive coaching during scored repetitions.
commonErrors.correction: Record the outcome and provide feedback after assessment.

commonErrors.error: Safety technique is overlooked because the player wins possession.
commonErrors.correction: Score unsafe entry or contact as a technical failure.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue affects later stations disproportionately.
commonErrors.correction: Balance station order and provide scheduled recovery.

commonErrors.error: Scores lack written context.
commonErrors.correction: Record a brief observation explaining each major strength or limitation.

progressions: Repeat the assessment with match-like contact for appropriate senior groups.
regressions: Replace live contact with bump pads.
Assess technical elements separately before combining them.
matchApplication: Ground-ball effectiveness depends on safe contest entry, clean possession, protection, second effort and connection with teammates. This assessment measures whether players can apply those behaviours under realistic pressure rather than only in unopposed technical work.

title: Half-Forward Ground-Ball Reset and Re-Entry
primarySkill: Retaining possession after a half-forward ground-ball win and creating a second forward entry
objective: Develop the ability to avoid a rushed forward entry after winning a ground ball at half-forward, reset possession through support and re-enter inside 50 to a better-positioned target.
groundSize: Half-forward area approximately forty metres wide and thirty-five metres long, including the inside-50 arc where available.
setup:
Mark a ground-ball recovery zone near half-forward.
Position one collector and one passive defender in the zone.
Place two reset players behind and across the ground.
Position two forwards inside 50.
Mark left, central and right entry gates.
The coach sends a low or rolling football into the recovery zone.
The first forward option is initially restricted to encourage a reset.
Rotate midfield, reset and forward roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach delivers the football into the half-forward recovery zone.
The collector wins possession under passive pressure.
The direct inside-50 option is shown as closed.
The collector releases backwards or laterally to a reset player.
The reset player transfers possession across the ground or to a second support player.
Forwards adjust their leading patterns as the football changes side.
The reset player identifies the best re-entry gate.
The football is kicked inside 50 to a leading target.
The original collector follows the reset and remains underneath the entry.
The sequence ends when a forward marks or the defence wins possession.
coachingPoints: Winning possession does not require an immediate forward entry.
Protect the football before resetting.
Reset players must remain behind and outside congestion.
Move the football far enough to change the defensive angle.
Forwards should reset their leads rather than continuing towards closed space.
The re-entry kick must target advantage.
The original collector supports underneath.
Maintain defensive balance in case of turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the collector recognises the closed direct option.
Whether possession is retained safely.
Whether reset players maintain useful width.
Whether the switch changes the entry angle.
Whether forwards stop and re-lead.
Whether the final kick targets the correct space.
Whether the original collector follows.
Whether the team retains turnover protection.

commonErrors.error: The collector kicks blindly inside 50.
commonErrors.correction: Recognise the closed option and use the reset.

commonErrors.error: Reset players stand too close to the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width and depth behind possession.

commonErrors.error: The reset disposal does not change the angle.
commonErrors.correction: Move the football farther laterally before re-entry.

commonErrors.error: Forwards continue leading into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Stop, reorganise and lead into the new entry lane.

commonErrors.error: The final kick is directed at a stationary target.
commonErrors.correction: Kick into the forward’s movement path.

commonErrors.error: All players move ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain support and defensive cover underneath.

progressions: Allow the collector to enter directly when the option is genuinely open.
Continue through to a shot at goal.
regressions: Mark the re-entry gate before the sequence begins.
successIndicators: Recognise when the direct entry is unavailable.
Retain possession after the ground-ball win.
matchApplication: Half-forward ground-ball wins often tempt players into rushed inside-50 kicks. Resetting possession can shift defenders, improve forward leading space and create a higher-quality scoring opportunity.
relatedDrills: GB-027 – Ground-Ball Win to Moving Lead
GB-036 – Ground-Ball Win to Square-Up Kick

title: Team Ground-Ball Movement Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing team structure and ball movement following ground-ball wins
objective: Assess whether players can organise effectively around ground-ball contests, secure possession, connect through appropriate team structures and maintain balance during attack and defence.
groundSize: Five assessment stations across approximately half an oval, plus one continuous team game area.
setup:
Establish five structured assessment stations:
Station 1: Centre-square ground-ball exit.
Station 2: Wing win and opposite-side transfer.
Station 3: Support behind and redirect.
Station 4: Defensive 50 to midfield rebound.
Station 5: Ground-ball win to forward connection.
Finish with a continuous transition game.
Assign coaches to assess individual role execution and team structure.
Use consistent starting positions, feeds and pressure levels.
Provide one familiarisation repetition at each station.
Record technical, tactical, communication and transition outcomes separately.
Balance station order to manage fatigue.
howTheDrillWorks:
Groups rotate through the five structured stations.
Each group completes three scored repetitions per station.
Players receive no coaching during scored repetitions.
Coaches assess the initial ground-ball win and the complete possession chain.
A repetition ends when possession reaches the target, exits the area or turns over.
After all stations, teams complete two timed blocks of continuous transition play.
The coach restarts every phase with a ground ball.
Team scores are awarded for clean possession, effective structure and successful transition.
Individual observations are recorded immediately.
Results are reviewed after the complete assessment.
coachingPoints: Standardise pressure, space and feeding conditions.
Assess organisation before possession as well as skill execution.
Record whether players maintain inside and outside roles.
Evaluate support behind the football.
Assess whether the first disposal escapes pressure.
Record width, stagger and forward connection.
Evaluate immediate reaction after turnovers.
Do not reward successful outcomes created through poor or unsafe structure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Role allocation before the ground-ball contest.
Technical quality of the initial collection.
Outside support and width.
Support depth behind possession.
Accuracy and timing of the first disposal.
Staggered forward-running options.
Field-position-specific decision making.
Communication throughout the chain.
Team balance behind the football.
Turnover reaction and defensive transition.

commonErrors.error: Coaches assess only whether the team reaches the final target.
commonErrors.correction: Evaluate organisation, collection, support and transition throughout the sequence.

commonErrors.error: Pressure levels vary between groups.
commonErrors.correction: Use consistent defender roles and contact restrictions.

commonErrors.error: Individual observations are lost inside team scoring.
commonErrors.correction: Record player role execution separately from the team result.

commonErrors.error: Players are coached during scored repetitions.
commonErrors.correction: Provide feedback after the station or assessment block.

commonErrors.error: Later groups are disadvantaged by fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Balance station order and schedule recovery.

commonErrors.error: A successful disposal hides poor team spacing.
commonErrors.correction: Score structure and outcome as separate measures.

commonErrors.error: Unsafe contact is overlooked because possession is retained.
commonErrors.correction: Record unsafe technique as a failed criterion.

progressions: Repeat the assessment with match-like contact.
Compare results across multiple training phases.
regressions: Assess three stations rather than five.
Assess technical collection separately before team movement.
successIndicators: Organise effective inside and outside roles.
Maintain width, depth and support behind the football.
Move the first disposal beyond pressure.
Connect possession according to field position.
Maintain technical and tactical quality under fatigue.
matchApplication: Team ground-ball performance depends on more than the player who wins possession. This assessment measures whether the entire group can organise around the contest, provide the correct support, move possession effectively and react when the football changes hands.

title: Advanced Ground-Ball Decision Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing advanced ground-ball decision making under deception, changing pressure, numerical imbalance and tactical risk
objective: Assess whether players can secure ground-ball possession and apply the correct tactical response when exits, numbers, pressure and support change unpredictably.
groundSize: Five assessment stations across approximately half an oval, plus one dynamic game area.
setup:
Establish five assessment stations:
Station 1: Deceptive pickup and defender manipulation.
Station 2: Late-closing outlet decision.
Station 3: One-versus-two survival.
Station 4: Exit risk matrix.
Station 5: Tempo control after possession.
Finish with the dynamic numbers ground-ball game.
Assign trained observers to every station.
Standardise starting positions, feeds and contact restrictions.
Give each player one familiarisation repetition.
Record decision quality and skill execution separately.
Manage fatigue so later stations remain valid.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players rotate through the five structured stations.
Each player completes three scored repetitions per station.
Coaches do not provide technical feedback during scored repetitions.
The player must respond to the live defensive and support picture.
Each repetition ends with a controlled exit, retention, turnover or neutral result.
Observers score scanning, collection, decision, execution and transition.
After the stations, teams complete two timed blocks of dynamic-numbers play.
Individual and team decisions are recorded during the game.
Results are reviewed after the full assessment.
Scores are used to identify technical, tactical and role-specific development needs.
coachingPoints: Standardise pressure while allowing genuine decisions.
Assess scanning before possession.
Separate collection quality from tactical choice.
Record whether the player updates the decision when information changes.
Reward retention or neutralisation when aggressive exit is unrealistic.
Assess tempo selection.
Evaluate risk against likely reward.
Record transition reaction after possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Pre-collection scanning.
Technical quality of the ground-ball win.
Ball protection under pressure.
Recognition of late outlet closure.
Decision making when outnumbered.
Use of deception.
Selection of corridor, wide or retention exits.
Tempo control after possession.
Communication with support.
Transition response after turnover.

commonErrors.error: Observers score only whether possession is retained.
commonErrors.correction: Assess scanning, decision quality and execution separately.

commonErrors.error: Defender behaviour varies significantly between players.
commonErrors.correction: Standardise defender starting rules and pressure limits.

commonErrors.error: Safe neutral decisions are scored as failures.
commonErrors.correction: Reward correct risk management in outnumbered situations.

commonErrors.error: Players receive coaching during scored repetitions.
commonErrors.correction: Provide feedback only after the station or assessment.

commonErrors.error: Later scores are reduced by unmanaged fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Balance station order and schedule recovery.

commonErrors.error: A successful outcome hides a poor decision.
commonErrors.correction: Score process and result as separate criteria.

commonErrors.error: Written observations are too general.
commonErrors.correction: Record the exact cue missed, decision made and execution outcome.

progressions: Remove marked gates and visual cues.
Compare results across multiple training blocks.
regressions: Assess decision components separately before combining them.
matchApplication: Advanced ground-ball performance requires more than winning possession. Players must process changing pressure, support, numbers and field risk while maintaining technical control. This assessment measures whether those decisions remain effective under realistic complexity.

title: Ground-Ball Win to Immediate Defensive Press
Rotating-Pressure Ground-Ball Chain
primarySkill: Maintaining possession as pressure rotates around successive receivers
objective: Develop the ability to identify changing pressure angles and maintain a possession chain when a new defender closes each receiver.
groundSize: Circular or square area approximately twenty-five metres across.
setup:
Mark a central ground-ball zone.
Position four attacking receivers around the outside.
Place one attacker as the initial collector.
Position three defenders at different numbered gates.
The coach calls a defender number after every disposal.
The nominated defender closes the next receiver.
Attackers must move possession away from the rotating pressure.
A successful chain requires four retained disposals.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach rolls the football to the central collector.
The player gathers and releases to an outside receiver.
The coach calls the first pressure number.
The nominated defender closes the receiver.
Other attackers reposition to provide new options.
The receiver protects possession and disposes away from pressure.
A different defender is called after the next disposal.
The chain continues until four disposals are completed or possession turns over.
If defenders win the football, they attack a central scoring gate.
Players rotate collector, receiver and defender roles.
coachingPoints: Scan before receiving.
Recognise which pressure player has become active.
Move support away from the closing defender.
The receiver should protect possession before disposing.
Avoid returning the football towards the pressure source.
Use quick disposal only when the target is ready.
Maintain one support option behind possession.
Non-active defenders remain positioned but do not interfere.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether receivers scan before possession.
Whether the active defender is identified.
Whether support players adjust promptly.
Whether the receiver protects the football.
Whether disposal moves away from pressure.
Whether the chain maintains spacing.
Whether rear support remains available.
Whether defenders rotate safely and realistically.

commonErrors.error: The receiver waits until possession to locate pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Scan before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Support players remain stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Reposition as soon as the new defender is called.

commonErrors.error: The football is returned towards the active defender.
commonErrors.correction: Transfer away from the pressure source.

commonErrors.error: The receiver rushes disposal to an unprepared teammate.
commonErrors.correction: Protect possession until a clear target presents.

commonErrors.error: All support moves ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Retain one option behind possession.

commonErrors.error: Non-active defenders interfere with the phase.
commonErrors.correction: Hold position until nominated.

progressions: Remove the numbered call and let defenders activate independently.
Continue into a scoring transition after the chain.
regressions: Allow attackers to remain at fixed gates.
successIndicators: Move the football away from pressure.
matchApplication: Pressure shifts rapidly as defenders rotate, hand over opponents and close different receivers. Players must continually update their awareness rather than relying on the defensive picture from the previous possession.

title: Chaos Ground Ball to Controlled Possession
Key Forward Ground-Ball Recovery and Release
primarySkill: Recovering a ground ball as a key forward and releasing to a smaller support player
objective: Develop the ability of a key forward to recover after an incomplete marking contest, secure or protect the ground ball and release to a teammate in a better finishing position.
groundSize: Forward-50 contest area approximately twenty-five metres long and twenty metres wide.
setup:
Position a key forward and key defender in a marking contest.
Place two small forwards outside the landing area.
Position one additional defender at ground level.
The coach delivers the football to the aerial contest.
The mark is spoiled or allowed to spill.
The key forward must recover and assess whether to collect, protect or direct the football.
Small forwards move through receive gates.
Rotate aerial and ground-level roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach delivers the football to the marking contest.
The key forward competes in the air.
The football spills to ground.
The forward lands and locates the football.
The player competes with the key defender for recovery position.
If clean possession is available, the forward gathers and protects.
A small forward communicates and moves past the contest.
The key forward handballs or directs the football to the small forward.
The receiver finishes at goal.
If defenders win possession, forwards apply immediate pressure.
coachingPoints: Recover immediately after the aerial contest.
Use body size and strength legally to protect the drop zone.
Take clean possession when possible.
Do not attempt to turn through multiple defenders unnecessarily.
Small forwards must remain outside the key forward’s feet.
Release into the runner’s path.
Continue protecting or shepherding after disposal.
Apply forward pressure after turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the key forward lands safely.
Whether the spill is located immediately.
Whether body position protects the football.
Whether possession is taken when available.
Whether small forwards remain outside congestion.
Whether the release leads the receiver.
Whether the key forward continues supporting.
Whether defensive pressure follows turnover.

commonErrors.error: The key forward remains focused on the missed mark.
commonErrors.correction: Recover immediately and locate the ground ball.

commonErrors.error: The player attempts to turn through several defenders.
commonErrors.correction: Protect possession and release to outside support.

commonErrors.error: Small forwards crowd the key forward’s feet.
commonErrors.correction: Hold outside positions and arrive after the spill.

commonErrors.error: The handball is delivered behind the runner.
commonErrors.correction: Lead the small forward into scoring space.

commonErrors.error: The key forward stops after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Shepherd, block legally or remain available.

commonErrors.error: Forwards stop working after defenders win possession.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate pressure and protect the central exit.

progressions: Allow the aerial contest to be fully live.
Allow the key forward to finish when space opens.
Continue into a front-half pressure game.
successIndicators: Recover immediately after the aerial contest.
Release accurately to a smaller forward.
matchApplication: Key forwards do not complete every marking opportunity. Their ability to recover, protect the spill and release to smaller teammates can turn an incomplete aerial contest into a scoring opportunity.

title: Goal-Line Ground-Ball Scramble
primarySkill: Defending and resolving a loose-football scramble immediately in front of goal
objective: Develop the ability of defenders to protect the goal line, organise roles and either secure, clear or safely neutralise a loose football during a high-pressure goal-square scramble.
groundSize: Goal square and an area extending approximately fifteen metres from goal.
setup:
Position three defenders and three forwards around the goal square.
Place one support player from each team outside the immediate contest.
Mark two defensive exit gates on either side of the goal square.
The coach begins each phase with a rolling, bouncing, spoiled or deflected football inside the scoring area.
Defenders must maintain at least one player between the football and goal.
Forwards attempt to gain possession and score.
Match-like legal contact is permitted for appropriately prepared players.
Rotate players through last-line, support and pressure roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces the football into the goal-square area.
Defenders immediately organise goal-side, ball-pressure and outlet roles.
Forwards attack the loose football and attempt to create a scoring action.
The nearest defender contests the football.
A second defender protects the goal line.
The third defender provides an exit or support option.
If the defence wins possession, it attempts to exit through either gate.
If clean possession is unavailable, defenders may legally knock the football towards safety or create a controlled stoppage.
Forwards apply repeat pressure until possession exits, a score occurs or the coach stops play.
The group resets with a different initial spill.
coachingPoints: Protect the goal line before chasing the football.
Allocate one defender to the ball and one to dangerous space.
Avoid all defenders diving into the same contest.
Secure possession when cleanly available.
Use the boundary side or outside support when central exits are unsafe.
Do not handball blindly across the face of goal.
Maintain legal contact around players over the football.
Continue defending after the first clearance attempt.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether defenders organise immediately.
Whether the goal line remains protected.
Whether only the required players enter the contest.
Whether clean possession is taken when available.
Whether dangerous central disposal is avoided.
Whether forwards sustain legal pressure.
Whether defenders communicate the safest exit.
Whether repeat efforts continue after spills and smothers.

commonErrors.error: Every defender attacks the football and leaves goal exposed.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one ball-pressure player and retain goal-line cover.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner handballs blindly into central space.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm a clear receiver or use a safer outside exit.

commonErrors.error: Defenders knock away a football that could be secured.
commonErrors.correction: Take clean possession when balanced and protected.

commonErrors.error: Players dive head-first into a crowded goal-square contest.
commonErrors.correction: Stay balanced, protect the head and enter from a safer angle.

commonErrors.error: Forwards stop after the first failed scoring attempt.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate repeat pressure and remain goal side of exits.

commonErrors.error: Defenders celebrate the clearance before possession is safe.
commonErrors.correction: Continue supporting until the football leaves the defensive area.

progressions: Begin from a live marking contest.
Continue into a full defensive rebound.
regressions: Begin with two defenders and two forwards.
Stop after the first clean defensive possession.
successIndicators: Win or neutralise dangerous ground balls.
matchApplication: Loose footballs near the goal line create immediate scoring danger. Defenders must protect the line, remain composed and resolve the contest without every player being drawn towards the football.

title: Boundary Throw-In Ground-Ball Escape
primarySkill: Extracting a ground ball from a boundary throw-in contest
objective: Develop the ability to organise inside and outside roles at a boundary stoppage, win the resulting ground ball and move possession away from the boundary congestion.
groundSize: Boundary-side stoppage area approximately twenty-five metres long and twenty metres wide.
setup:
Position two rucks and two inside players from each team near the boundary.
Place one outside player from each team inboard of the contest.
Mark two inboard outlet gates and one down-the-line gate.
The coach conducts a controlled boundary throw-in or simulated tap.
Inside players compete for the resulting ground ball.
Outside players must remain clear of the initial congestion.
Teams attack opposite directions along the boundary line.
Rotate ruck, inside and outside roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach initiates the boundary throw-in.
Rucks compete and direct the football towards the stoppage area.
Inside players compete for the ground ball.
Outside players adjust according to the tap and defensive positioning.
The ball winner secures and protects possession.
The player selects an inboard, down-the-line or retention exit.
Outside support receives beyond the immediate tackle zone.
The possession team attempts to carry or dispose through a scoring gate.
If possession changes, teams reverse roles immediately.
The phase resets after an exit, turnover or secondary stoppage.
coachingPoints: Recognise the reduced space created by the boundary.
Maintain at least one inboard outlet.
Inside players should not all chase the same tap line.
Secure possession before attempting the release.
Avoid blind handballs towards the boundary line.
Use the down-the-line option only when it gains territory safely.
Outside support should receive facing the field.
Transition immediately after possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players organise around the boundary restriction.
Whether outside support remains inboard.
Whether the ground ball is secured.
Whether the first disposal leaves congestion.
Whether the receiver faces forward.
Whether the boundary is used safely.
Whether defenders protect central space.
Whether repeat efforts continue after secondary spills.

commonErrors.error: All players stand on the boundary side of the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Preserve an inboard receiver and central defensive cover.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner handballs towards the line without a target.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm the receiver or retain possession.

commonErrors.error: Outside players move into the initial stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Hold beyond congestion until possession is established.

commonErrors.error: The down-the-line disposal is used despite heavy numbers.
commonErrors.correction: Use the inboard or rear option when the boundary route is blocked.

commonErrors.error: The receiver collects while facing the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the starting angle to receive facing the field.

commonErrors.error: Players stop when the first extraction fails.
commonErrors.correction: Reorganise around the secondary ground-ball contest.

progressions: Add another outside player per team.
regressions: Simulate the tap with a coach roll.
successIndicators: Organise effectively at the boundary stoppage.
Secure or neutralise the ground ball.
matchApplication: Boundary throw-ins compress numbers and limit available space. Effective teams maintain an inboard outlet and avoid allowing every player to become trapped between the football and boundary.

title: Forward 50 Repeat-Entry Ground-Ball Scenario
primarySkill: Winning a forward-50 ground ball and creating a repeat scoring entry
objective: Develop the ability to retain front-half possession after a spilled or intercepted entry and create a second, higher-quality scoring opportunity.
groundSize: Forward 50 and an area extending approximately twenty metres beyond the arc.
setup:
Position forwards and defenders inside 50.
Place attacking midfielders outside the contest as front-half support.
Begin each phase with an inside-50 kick designed to be spoiled, intercepted incompletely or brought to ground.
Mark two defensive rebound gates.
Mark reset and re-entry gates for the attacking team.
The attacking team attempts to win the ground ball and create another entry.
Defenders attempt to exit the area.
Rotate forwards, defenders and midfield support roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach or midfielder delivers the initial inside-50 kick.
Defenders and forwards contest the entry.
The football is brought to ground.
The nearest attacker competes for possession.
Teammates protect likely defensive exits and provide support behind.
If the attacking team wins possession, it may finish immediately or reset outside the contest.
Forwards reorganise their leading patterns.
The football is re-entered through the best available gate.
If defenders gain possession, they attempt to exit through a rebound gate.
Play continues until a score, clean defensive exit or coach reset.
coachingPoints: One player attacks the ground ball while others protect rebound space.
Do not crowd the football with every forward.
Secure possession before attempting a repeat entry.
Use support behind when the immediate scoring lane is closed.
Forwards must reset and separate before the second entry.
Protect the corridor after losing possession.
Reward repeat pressure as well as scoring outcome.
Maintain defensive balance outside the contest.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether attackers divide ball-winning and lock-in roles.
Whether the ground ball is secured.
Whether support remains outside congestion.
Whether defensive exits are protected.
Whether the attacking team recognises when to reset.
Whether forwards reorganise before re-entry.
Whether the second entry improves scoring probability.
Whether defenders transition cleanly when they win possession.

commonErrors.error: All forwards collapse onto the ground ball.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one primary contestant and preserve outside pressure roles.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner attempts a blind shot under pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and use the reset when the scoring lane is closed.

commonErrors.error: Supporting midfielders move too close.
commonErrors.correction: Hold outside the contest and provide a clear re-entry platform.

commonErrors.error: Forwards continue old leads during the reset.
commonErrors.correction: Stop, separate and organise new leading patterns.

commonErrors.error: The attacking team protects the boundary but leaves the corridor open.
commonErrors.correction: Close the most dangerous central rebound first.

commonErrors.error: Players judge success only by whether a goal is scored.
commonErrors.correction: Assess ground-ball win, lock-in and quality of repeat entry.

progressions: Begin from different inside-50 entry angles.
regressions: Stop after the first repeat possession.
successIndicators: Win or neutralise the forward-50 ground ball.
