relatedDrills: GB-067 – Half-Forward Ground-Ball Reset and Re-Entry

title: Wet-Weather Ground-Ball Territory Game
primarySkill: Winning ground-ball territory and retaining structure in wet conditions
objective: Develop team behaviours suited to wet conditions, including secure collection, territorial decision making, repeat contests and simplified disposal.
groundSize: Rectangle approximately fifty metres long and thirty-five metres wide.
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Mark a scoring zone at each end.
Lightly wet the footballs while ensuring the playing surface remains safe.
Begin every phase with a rolling, bouncing or skidding football.
Teams score by carrying possession into the end zone or gaining controlled territory through a designated gate.
Award bonus points for clean wet-weather collection and repeat ground-ball wins.
Controlled tackling is permitted.
Stop immediately if the surface becomes unsafe.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces a wet football into the playing area.
Teams compete for possession.
The ball winner attempts to secure the football with two hands.
Teammates provide support behind and outside the contest.
The possession team selects a simple disposal or territorial option.
If possession spills, players complete an immediate second effort.
The defending team protects central space and applies pressure.
A team scores by reaching the end zone or completing the nominated territorial action.
A new wet ground ball is introduced after each score or stoppage.
Play continues for timed blocks with surface and football checks between blocks.
coachingPoints: Adjust approach speed for the skidding football.
Use soft hands and absorb the football into the body.
Expect fumbles and remain ready for a second effort.
Use simple handballs and lower-risk kicks.
Gain territory when clean possession cannot be maintained.
Maintain players behind the football.
Avoid overhandling in congestion.
Place player safety above drill intensity.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players adjust approach speed.
Whether two-hand collection is prioritised.
Whether the football is absorbed into the body.
Whether second efforts occur immediately.
Whether disposal choices suit the conditions.
Whether support remains behind possession.
Whether teams gain useful territory.
Whether footing and contact remain safe.

commonErrors.error: Players approach the skidding football at uncontrolled speed.
commonErrors.correction: Slow earlier and shorten the final steps.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner attempts intricate disposal in congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Use the simplest effective option.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after a fumble.
commonErrors.correction: Expect the spill and complete the next effort immediately.

commonErrors.error: Teams handball repeatedly without escaping pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Use territory or an outside exit when congestion remains.

commonErrors.error: All players move ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain support and defensive protection behind possession.

commonErrors.error: The drill continues despite unsafe footing.
commonErrors.correction: Stop, inspect the surface and modify or end the activity.

progressions: Continue into a larger match simulation.
Restrict the number of handballs before a territorial action.
matchApplication: Wet-weather football produces more ground-ball contests and fewer clean possession chains. Teams must simplify disposal, expect repeated spills and value territory without abandoning support structure.

title: Match Ground-Ball Audit Game
primarySkill: Auditing team ground-ball behaviour during extended match simulation
objective: Evaluate how consistently the team applies its ground-ball principles during realistic, extended and minimally interrupted match play.
groundSize: Full oval or three-quarter oval.
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Use realistic positional structures and interchange.
Play timed match-simulation blocks.
Coaches record ground-ball behaviours without stopping play except for safety.
Restart normal stoppages using centre bounces, boundary throw-ins, ball-ups or realistic loose-football feeds.
Assign observers to technical, structural, transition and positional categories.
Use scoreboard conditions appropriate to the training phase.
Review observations only between blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins under normal Australian football rules.
Coaches record every significant ground-ball contest.
Observers identify which team wins first possession.
They record whether the ball winner secures, protects and disposes effectively.
Team structure around the contest is assessed.
Transition after possession gain or loss is recorded.
Positional responsibilities are assessed according to field location.
Play continues with minimal coach interruption.
Teams receive brief evidence-based feedback between blocks.
A final block tests whether identified behaviours improve.
coachingPoints: Avoid coaching every individual contest during play.
Observe what players do without immediate instruction.
Record both possession result and process.
Assess numbers inside and outside the contest.
Record support behind the football.
Evaluate the first disposal after the win.
Assess defensive reaction after loss.
Compare behaviour across different field positions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Contest entry and safety.
Clean collection percentage.
Ball protection after possession.
Number of players entering the contest.
Outside and rear support.
First-disposal effectiveness.
Repeat efforts after spills.
Positional decision making.
Communication.
Transition after possession changes.
Performance under fatigue.
Improvement between blocks.

commonErrors.error: Coaches interrupt too often to correct errors.
commonErrors.correction: Record patterns and provide feedback between blocks.

commonErrors.error: Observers record only who wins the football.
commonErrors.correction: Assess collection, support, disposal and transition.

commonErrors.error: Different observers use inconsistent standards.
commonErrors.correction: Agree on definitions and scoring criteria before play.

commonErrors.error: Players alter behaviour because every contest is verbally assessed.
commonErrors.correction: Keep observation discreet and allow realistic play.

commonErrors.error: Feedback is too broad to guide improvement.
commonErrors.correction: Use specific examples and measurable patterns.

commonErrors.error: The final block repeats the same errors without a focus.
commonErrors.correction: Give each line one or two clear behavioural targets.

regressions: Assess only two or three ground-ball behaviours.
Stop once per block for guided correction.
matchApplication: Extended match simulation reveals whether ground-ball behaviours remain reliable when players are fatigued, under scoreboard pressure and required to organise without constant coach intervention.

title: Ground-Ball Chapter Final Assessment
primarySkill: Completing a comprehensive assessment of individual and team ground-ball performance
objective: Provide a final structured assessment covering the complete Ground Balls chapter, from fundamental collection through movement, pressure, team structure, advanced decisions and match application.
groundSize: Six assessment stations across half an oval, followed by a three-quarter or full-ground assessment game.
setup:
Establish six assessment stations:
Station 1: Fundamental collection and body position.
Station 2: Moving pickup, exit and disposal.
Station 3: Pressure, contact and second effort.
Station 4: Team outlet and transition structure.
Station 5: Advanced decision and risk selection.
Station 6: Position-specific match scenario.
Scale contact, distance and complexity according to age and ability.
Assign trained observers to every station.
Provide one familiarisation repetition before scoring.
Finish with an extended match-simulation audit game.
Score individual technique and team performance separately.
Standardise feeds, pressure and criteria.
Schedule recovery between high-load stations.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players rotate through all six assessment stations.
Each player completes three scored repetitions at every station.
Coaches assess the complete action before, during and after possession.
No technical coaching is given during scored repetitions.
Individual scores cover collection, balance, protection, scanning, decision and disposal.
Team scores cover role allocation, support, communication and transition.
After station assessment, players complete timed match-simulation blocks.
Every significant ground-ball contest is audited during the game.
Results from stations and match simulation are compared.
Coaches produce individual and team development priorities from the combined assessment.
coachingPoints: Use age-appropriate contact and complexity.
Assess technical fundamentals before tactical outcome.
Record whether the player reaches the correct football line.
Evaluate movement and balance after collection.
Assess performance under pressure and contact.
Record support recognition and disposal choice.
Evaluate team organisation around the contest.
Compare controlled-station performance with match transfer.
Record strengths as well as deficiencies.
Stop any activity where fatigue compromises safety.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Approach line and speed.
Body position at collection.
Two-hand security.
Balance and momentum.
Ball protection.
Pre-collection and post-collection scanning.
Decision making under pressure.
Disposal legality and effectiveness.
Second effort.
Inside and outside role organisation.
Support behind possession.
Communication.
Positional responsibility.
Transition after possession change.
Technical transfer into match simulation.

commonErrors.error: Assessment conditions vary significantly between groups.
commonErrors.correction: Standardise feeds, space, contact and scoring before beginning.

commonErrors.error: Coaches assess only the final possession outcome.
commonErrors.correction: Score the complete process from approach through transition.

commonErrors.error: Players receive coaching during scored repetitions.
commonErrors.correction: Record the issue and provide feedback after assessment.

commonErrors.error: Technical and tactical errors are combined into one score.
commonErrors.correction: Record collection, decision and execution separately.

commonErrors.error: Match-simulation observations are not linked to station results.
commonErrors.correction: Compare controlled performance with live-game transfer.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue invalidates later results.
commonErrors.correction: Balance station order and provide sufficient recovery.

commonErrors.error: Younger or developing players face excessive complexity.
commonErrors.correction: Scale contact, numbers, distances and decisions appropriately.

commonErrors.error: Feedback identifies weaknesses without development priorities.
commonErrors.correction: Convert results into specific technical and team training targets.

progressions: Repeat under wet conditions where safe.
Remove marked gates and visual cues.
Compare results with competition statistics and video.
Repeat the assessment at defined seasonal checkpoints.
regressions: Assess four stations rather than six.
Separate technical and tactical assessment across different sessions.
successIndicators: Transfer station performance into match play.
matchApplication: The final assessment determines whether players can transfer the complete ground-ball skill set into realistic Australian football. It identifies technical, tactical, physical and team-structure priorities for future training.
relatedDrills: GB-060 – Ground-Ball Pressure and Contest Assessment
